rounds.text: Siddha Ventures Ltd trades at a severe and unwarranted discount to its underlying asset base, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.27x on a book value of ₹ 14.6 [E1], which is further underscored by a provider-reported P/B of 0.25x against a sector benchmark of 1.32x [E6]. This deep asset discount exists alongside an attractive earnings multiple, as the stock commands a P/E of 12.67x that sits well below the sector benchmark of 19.49x [E5]. Operational efficiency also merits recognition, with the company delivering a return on assets of 1.93% that manages to slightly edge out the sector benchmark of 1.86% [E7]. Historical top-line performance demonstrates substantial medium-term expansion, evidenced by a compounded sales growth rate of 52% over 5 years and 23% over 10 years [E13, E14]. Conceded: the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E3], the stock sits low in its 52-week range [E4], and compounded sales growth has contracted by 7% over 3 years [E15] as well as 71% over the trailing twelve months [E16].

The bull case of deep discounting falls apart when examining the severe, recent contraction in top-line performance. Compounded sales growth has cratered to -7% over 3 years [E15] and collapsed by an alarming -71% over the trailing twelve months [E16]. Furthermore, investors receive zero income return from holding this asset, evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. Trading at 20% of its 52-week range [E4], the depressed price of ₹ 4.01 [E1] and tiny market capitalisation of ₹ 4.01 Cr [E2] reflect a lack of market confidence rather than a genuine bargain. Conceded: [E7].

Conceded: [E15] and [E16]. While those top-line contraction figures are real, the bear ignores the accelerating bottom-line reality where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 143% and earnings growth is actively accelerating [E46, E57]. This profit momentum triggered a specific screen reason for profit growth above 20% YoY [E55], proving that operational efficiency matters far more than shrinking top-line revenues during this phase. The bear complains about a 0.00% dividend yield [E3], but retaining all earnings directly fuels the exceptionally cheap valuation multiples, such as a price-to-book ratio of 0.25x against a sector benchmark of 1.32x [E6]. Furthermore, dismissing the market capitalisation of ₹ 4.01 Cr [E2] ignores the fundamental safety margin of buying assets at 0.27x book value [E1] while simultaneously generating a return on assets of 1.93% that outperforms the sector benchmark of 1.86% [E7].
